question: After temporal tracking and final memory compression are learned in stages, can the complete history module be jointly fine-tuned without losing cup identity?

initialization.stage_1: Train the fixed-grid temporal tracker without the final learned memory bottleneck; final validation accuracy 100%.
initialization.stage_2: Freeze the successful temporal tracker and train the 128-token final memory compressor and classifier; final validation accuracy 100%.

stage_3.description: Load the successful Stage 2 checkpoint, unfreeze the complete fixed-grid temporal and final-memory history module, and jointly fine-tune it at one tenth of the original learning rate.

conclusion.evidence: All four full-validation evaluations remained at 100% accuracy; the final classifier loss was 1.94e-6 and final memory-token diversity loss remained finite at 0.0183.
conclusion.scope_limit: This validates the staged optimization schedule for the one-swap cup-identity classification diagnostic. It does not yet prove that the same schedule succeeds under Pi0 action loss or in closed-loop robot execution.
conclusion.next_step: Translate the same three-stage curriculum to action training: establish the temporal path under an easy or residual action interface, train the final memory/action interface with the temporal path frozen, then jointly fine-tune the history module at a reduced learning rate.
